text: Split the property-law criterion out as P6f.34 (bd-01KZ4CP2PWRN4MKP96808P4HV6), following the P6f.30 precedent. P6f.23 still blocks this bead and that block is right for the naming, fixture and compatibility criteria: hand-owning every field name while a new JobRequest field is inbound would do the work twice. It is not right for the laws. A round-trip law is written against whatever field set exists and keeps passing as fields are added, and P6f.23 adding a field is exactly the event it should catch if a codec forgets it. Holding the laws behind P6f.23 leaves the reportedCluster bug class unguarded for no benefit. The bounds asymmetry recorded here on 2026-08-03 goes with the laws, since check-before-allocate is what the bounds law asserts. Remaining here: owned stable field names and discriminators, language-neutral goldens for every agent method, and compatibility ownership of intentional format changes.
